text.p: Robert Fleming & Co Ltd said it has reduced its investment opinion on Brazilian cement firm Cimento Itau to long-term buy from buy following the release of weaker-than-expected first-quarter earnings results.
-- "Although the long-term, fundamental outlook for the company remains attractive, the short-term outlook has been clouded," Flemings' analyst Ben Uglow said in a report.

-- He said a complaint lodged against Votorantim group citing "anti-competitive practices," while unlikely to be adverse given Brazil's low cement prices, could hinder the speed and magnitude of further price increases.
-- Uglow also said changes to the country's IOF financial transaction tax, despigned to reduce consumer spending, could temper demand because cement is a consumer product in Brazil.
-- Flemings has adjusted its earnings forecasts to reflect higher operating costs, projecting net revenues to rise 1.0 percent to 391.8 million in fiscal 1997.

-- It also forecast a net profit of 40.1 million reais, down from a projected 52.4 million reais, and a new target of 15.5 reais a share. Cimento Itau posted a first-quarter net profit of 2.4 reais a share.
-- The shares have appreciated by 43.7 percent in absolute terms but underperformed the Ibovespa .BVSP by 19.3 percent in relative terms since August 1, 1996.
-- Cimento Itau's preferred was off 2.12 percent to 346 reais and its common was flat at 260 reais at 1450 local/1750 gmt in Sao Paulo.
